quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 40 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: Before riding, check your motorcycle's clutch. A working clutch should feel:

options.text: Loose and rough.
Tight and smooth.
Loose and smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tight and smooth.
questions.explanation: Check your clutch and throttle before riding. The throttle should snap back when released. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Decrease your following distance.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, increase your following distance. Slow down and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: When a driver makes eye contact with you:

options.text: They see you.
It will never happen.
It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield. Drivers often look at motorcyclists but do not consciously notice them.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: The pavement is slippery.
The sun is shining.
You expect normal stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle will take longer to stop. This includes slippery pavement, poor visibility, or heavy traffic.

questions.question: When reacting to a road hazard, do not:

options.text: Avoid communicating with other drivers.
Adjust your speed accordingly.
Use your horn, lights, or signals to alert others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid communicating with other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tell other drivers you are there by using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed and lane position as needed for safety.

questions.question: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because:

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
Other drivers can easily see you.
You may not be able to read road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous. The vehicle could swerve into your lane or block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris collect in the ______ of a lane.

options.text: left portion
middle portion
right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: middle portion
questions.explanation: Oil and debris from cars and trucks collect in the center of a lane.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle in a curve?

options.text: The outside of the curve
The inside of the curve
Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Each curve is different. Choose your lane position based on traffic and road conditions, and adjust as needed.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
You have space to maneuver.
You have limited escape route options.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have limited escape route options.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you time to react and room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, you should:

options.text: Speed up before hitting it.
Stay seated so the seat cushions the impact.
Approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down and approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to start moving.
Change to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have time to react to hazards.
You have space to maneuver.
You have more time to speed up when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to speed up when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle helps you react quickly and maneuver if another driver makes a mistake. This is important for safety.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
As soon as the truck is behind you.
When you feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only return to your lane when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: No parking is allowed.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what is the best way to ride your motorcycle?

options.text: Get off the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, avoid riding in the center of the lane where oil builds up. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by other cars. The left tire track is often safest.

questions.question: _________ of motorcycle and car crashes are caused by the driver not yielding the right-of-way to the motorcyclist.

options.text: One-quarter
More than half
One-half

questions.correctAnswerText: More than half
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car crashes happen because drivers fail to yield the right-of-way. Motorcyclists should never assume other drivers will yield, even if they are required to by law.

questions.question: You reach an unmarked intersection at the same time as another vehicle. What should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to tell the other vehicle to go.
Go through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an unmarked intersection with no traffic lights or signs, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what is the best way to ride?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull to the side of the road until the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the center of the lane becomes slippery with oil. Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars instead. The left tire track is often safest.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Only stop if other traffic is coming.
Vehicles will be entering the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: What color are service signs?

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. Services include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride under the speed limit.
Cover the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Accelerate before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When you approach a dangerous area like an intersection, cover the clutch lever and both brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
Both brakes are equally powerful.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid lines mean no passing. Dashed lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Perform both actions at the same time.
Only brake.
Perform one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Perform one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must both swerve and brake, do them one at a time. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Do not do both actions at the same time.

questions.question: The center of a lane has an oily strip. What about this strip?

options.text: Should be avoided at all times.
Usually provides enough grip for riding, unless it is raining.
Should only be used if you share the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually provides enough grip for riding, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip in the center of the road usually provides enough grip for safe riding, unless it rains. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so riders can generally ride on either side of it and still be in the center lane.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: Right
Center
Left

questions.correctAnswerText: Center
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when being passed. This is the safest position. Riding to the side of the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to cut back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may proceed through the intersection with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must come to a complete stop and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in the direction you want.

questions.question: Where do most motorcycle and car accidents happen?

options.text: At intersections.
On the open road.
In parking lots.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle and car crashes happen at intersections. The main cause is the car driver failing to give the right-of-way to the motorcyclist.

questions.question: If you have a passenger, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride at slower speeds than usual.
Allow more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle with a passenger handles differently because of the extra weight. Ride slower and allow more stopping distance. The passenger should hold firmly onto the passenger handgrips or onto your waist, hips, or midsection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: If another driver makes eye contact with you:

options.text: You know that they have seen you.
It doesn't always mean they've actually seen you.
They will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doesn't always mean they've actually seen you.
questions.explanation: Eye contact does not guarantee a driver has seen you. A driver may look directly at you but still not notice you.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle, you should position yourself:

options.text: To be seen in the vehicle's side mirror.
To be seen in the vehicle's rearview mirror.
To be seen through the vehicle's passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: To be seen in the vehicle's rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position your motorcycle in the center of your lane behind the car. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: Eye protection is:

options.text: Required for all riders.
Not required, but recommended.
Only required for inexperienced motorcycle users.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear eye protection on a moving motorcycle. A full face shield gives the best protection.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Choose a lane position that increases their visibility.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce their reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, choose a lane position that makes you visible to others. Have your hand near the clutch and brakes to react quickly. Slow down at intersections. Don't change your speed or position suddenly, as this may confuse other drivers.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should position your motorcycle:

options.text: In the outside of the curve.
In the inside of the curve.
Where you can most safely handle road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can most safely handle road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that works for the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In the front of the group.
At the tail end of the group.
Beside the lead rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way they won't fall behind, and experienced riders can watch them.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply the brake.
Release the front brake immediately and only use the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you come to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply the brake.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake right away. Then apply it again.

questions.question: In general, which position within a lane is the best to ride in?

options.text: The left position
The right position
There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Good riders change their position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best formation for keeping riders together while maintaining adequate space cushions is generally:

options.text: A single-file formation.
Riding in pairs.
A staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for a group of motorcyclists to stay together while giving each rider enough space to ride safely.
